source_text: Τὸ διὰ παντὸς εὖ πράττειν μόνου Θεοῦ· Σὺ δὲ, εἰ τοῖς παροῦ σιν ἀλγεῖς, ἀπὸ τῶν προλαβόντων σαυτὴν παραμύθησαι. Νῦν δακρύεις, ἀλλ' ἐγέλασας πρότερον· νῦν πτωχεύεις, ἀλλ' ἐπλούτησας πρότερον. Ἔπιες τὸ διειδὲς νᾶμα τοῦ βίου, καὶ τὸ θολερὸν τοῦτο πίνουσα καρτέρησον. Οὐδὲ τὰ τῶν ποταμῶν ῥεύματα διόλου φαίνεται καθαρά. Ποταμὸς δὲ, ὡς οἶσθα, ὁ βίος ἡμῶν, ῥέων ἐνδελεχῶς καὶ κύμασιν ἀλλεπαλλήλοις πληρού μενος. Τὸ μὲν γὰρ αὐτοῦ προέῤῥευσεν ἤδη, τὸ δὲ ἔτι πορεύεται· καὶ τὸ μὲν ἄρτι προέκυψε τῶν πηγῶν, τὸ δὲ μέλλει· καὶ πρὸς τὴν κοινὴν ἅπαντες τοῦ θανάτου σπεύδομεν θάλατταν. Εἰ τὰ ἀγαθὰ ἐδεξάμεθα ἐκ χειρὸς Κυρίου, τὰ κακὰ οὐχ ὑποίσομεν; Ἀναγκάζομεν τὸν κριτὴν ὅμοια χορηγεῖν πράγματα δι' αἰῶνος ἡμῖν; Διδάσκομεν τὸν Δεσπότην, ὅπως χρὴ διεξάγειν τὸν ἡμέτερον βίον; Αὐτὸς τῶν οἰκείων ψήφων ἔχει τὴν ἐξουσίαν. Ὅπως βούλεται τάττει τὰ καθ' ἡμᾶς. Σοφὸς δέ ἐστι, καὶ τὸ λυσιτελοῦν ἐπι μετρεῖ τοῖς οἰκέταις. Μὴ περιεργάζου τοῦ Δεσπότου τὴν κρίσιν. Ἀγάπα μόνον τὰ παρὰ τῆς αὐτοῦ σοφίας οἰκονομού μενα. Ὅπερ ἂν δῷ σοι, τοῦτο δέχου μεθ' ἡδονῆς. Δεῖξον ἐν τοῖς ἀλγεινοῖς, ὡς καὶ τῆς εὐφροσύνης ἀξία τῆς πρόσθεν ἐτύγχανες. Ταῦτα ὁ Ἰὼβ λέγων, ἀπεκρούσατο καὶ ταύτην τοῦ διαβόλου τὴν προσβολὴν, καὶ τελείαν αὐτῷ τῆς ἥττης αἰσχύνην ἐπήγαγε. Τί οὖν ἐντεῦθεν συνέβαινεν; Ἔφυγε αὖθις ἡ νόσος αὐτὸν, ὡς εἰκῆ προσελθοῦσα, καὶ μηδὲν ἀνύσασα πλέον. Ἀνέθαλεν εἰς δευτέραν ἥβην ἡ σάρξ· ἤνθησεν ὁ βίος πάλιν πᾶσι τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς, καὶ διπλασίων ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον πανταχόθεν ὁ πλοῦτος συνέῤῥευσεν, ἵνα τὸ μὲν ὡς μηδὲν ἀπολωλεκὼς ἔχῃ, τὸ δὲ ὑπάρξῃ τῆς καρτερίας τῷ δικαίῳ μισθός. Διὰ τί δὲ ἵππους μὲν, καὶ ἡμιόνους, καὶ καμήλους, καὶ πρόβατα, καὶ γεώργια, καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν τῆς περιουσίας τρυφὴν ἐκ τοῦ διπλασίονος ὑπ εδέξατο, ὁ τῶν παίδων δὲ ἀριθμὸς ἴσος τοῖς ἀποθανοῦσιν ἐβλάστησεν; Ὅτι τὰ μὲν ἄλογα κτήνη, καὶ πᾶς ὁ πλοῦτος διαφθειρόμενος, εἰς τελείαν ἦλθεν ἀπώλειαν· οἱ παῖδες δὲ, καὶ τεθνεῶτες, ἔζων τῷ καλλίστῳ μέρει τῆς φύσεως. Κοσμηθεὶς οὖν αὖθις ἑτέροις υἱοῖς καὶ θυγατράσιν ὑπὸ τοῦ κτίσαντος, καὶ τοῦτο εἶχε κτῆμα διπλοῦν. Οἱ μὲν γὰρ παρῆσαν τὴν ἐν τῷ βίῳ τοῖς γεννήσασιν εὐφροσύνην παρέχοντες, οἱ δὲ προ οδεύσαντες ἀνέμενον τὸν φυτεύσαντα· τότε πάντες περιστησόμενοι τὸν Ἰὼβ, ὅταν ὁ κριτὴς τῆς ἀνθρω πίνης ζωῆς συναγάγῃ τὴν Ἐκκλησίαν τὴν πάνδημον· ὅταν ἡ σάλπιγξ, ἡ τὴν τοῦ βασιλέως ἐπιδημίαν σημαίνουσα, τοῖς τάφοις σφοδρότερον ἐμβοήσασα, τὴν τῶν σωμάτων ἀπαιτήσῃ παρακαταθήκην. Τότε καὶ οἱ νῦν εἶναι δοκοῦντες νεκροὶ θᾶττον τῶν ζώντων παραστήσονται τῷ τῶν ὅλων δημιουργῷ. Διὰ τοῦτο, οἶμαι, διπλοῦν τὸν ἄλλον πλοῦτον ἐπιμετρήσας αὐτῷ, τοῖς παισὶν ἀρκεῖσθαι τοῖς ἴσοις αὐτὸν ἐδικαίωσεν. Ὁρᾷς ὁπόσα ὁ δίκαιος Ἰὼβ ἐκ τῆς ὑπομονῆς ἑαυτῷ συνέλεξεν ἀγαθά; Καὶ σὺ τοίνυν, εἴ τί σοι προσεπέλασε δυσχερὲς ἀπὸ τοῦ χθὲς ἀναφθέντος πυρὸς ἐκ τῆς τῶν δαιμόνων ἐπιβουλῆς, τοῦτο καρτέρησον, καὶ τὴν ἐκ τοῦ πάθους ἀνίαν κρείττοσι κατεύνασον λογισμοῖς· καὶ κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον, Ἐπίῤῥιψον ἐπὶ Κύριον τὴν μέριμνάν σου, καὶ αὐτός σε διαθρέψει. Αὐτῷ πρέπει ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: Job's endurance rewarded and the congregation urged to endure the fire
orientation: Basil is closing the homily, still speaking as Job to Job's wife, then turning to his congregation to apply Job's example to their own endurance after the recent fire.
pass_a_gloss: To do well always belongs to God alone. But you, if you are pained at the present things, comfort yourself from the things that went before. Now you weep, but you laughed before; now you are poor, but you were rich before. You drank the clear stream of life, and drinking this muddy one, endure. Not even the currents of rivers appear entirely clean. But a river, as you know, is our life, flowing continually and filled with waves one after another. For part of it has already flowed past, and part is still moving; and part has just gushed forth from the springs, and part is about to; and we all hasten toward the common sea of death. If we received good things from the Lord's hand, shall we not endure the bad things? Do we compel the judge to supply us with similar things forever? Do we teach the Master how he must conduct our life? He himself has authority over his own decrees. As he wishes he orders our affairs. But he is wise, and he measures out what is profitable to his servants. Do not meddle with the Master's judgment. Love only the things administered by his wisdom. Whatever he gives you, receive this with pleasure. Show in painful things that you were also worthy of the former gladness. Job, saying these things, repelled also this assault of the devil, and brought upon him the complete shame of defeat. What then followed from this? The disease fled from him again, as having come in vain and having accomplished nothing more. The flesh bloomed again into a second youth; life flowered again with all good things, and wealth flowed together doubled upon the house from every side, so that he might have the one part as having lost nothing, and the other part might be the reward of endurance for the righteous man. But why did he receive horses, and mules, and camels, and sheep, and fields, and all the luxury of his substance from the double, but the number of children sprouted equal to those who had died? Because the irrational beasts and all the wealth, being perishable, came to complete destruction; but the children, even having died, were alive in the fairest part of their nature. So, adorned again with other sons and daughters by the Creator, he had this possession also double. For the ones were present, providing gladness in life to their parents, and the ones who had gone before were waiting for the one who planted them; then all will stand around Job, when the judge of human life gathers the universal church; when the trumpet, signaling the arrival of the king, having shouted more violently into the tombs, demands back the deposit of bodies. Then also those who now seem to be dead will stand before the Creator of all things more quickly than the living. For this reason, I think, having measured out to him the other wealth double, he deemed it right for him to be satisfied with children equal in number. Do you see how many good things the righteous Job gathered for himself from endurance? You too, then, if anything difficult came near you from the fire kindled yesterday by the plot of the demons, endure this, and calm the grief from the suffering with better reasonings; and according to what is written, Cast your care upon the Lord, and he himself will nourish you. To him belongs glory forever and ever. Amen.

choices.why: Keeps the river imagery literal and vivid, matching the controlling image of life as a river in this passage.

choices.term: τὴν κοινὴν ἅπαντες τοῦ θανάτου σπεύδομεν θάλατταν
choices.english: we all hasten toward the common sea of death
choices.why: Preserves the metaphor of death as a sea into which the river of life flows, and the word 'common' for all humanity.
rejected: we all rush to the shared ocean of death
we all hurry toward the universal sea of death

choices.english: shall we not endure the bad things?
choices.why: Keeps the rhetorical question form and the plain contrast of good things and bad things, matching the Job quotation.
rejected: will we not bear the evils?
shall we not put up with the misfortunes?

choices.english: demands back the deposit of bodies
choices.why: Renders the legal metaphor of bodies as a deposit entrusted to the earth, which the trumpet calls back.

choices.term: Ἐπίῤῥιψον ἐπὶ Κύριον τὴν μέριμνάν σου
choices.english: Cast your care upon the Lord
choices.why: Follows the Psalm wording closely, using 'care' for merimna and the imperative 'cast' for epirripson.
rejected: Throw your anxiety upon the Lord
Hurl your worry onto the Lord

choices.english: the reward of endurance for the righteous man
choices.why: Uses the glossary term 'endurance' for karteria and keeps the dative of advantage clear.
rejected: the wage of fortitude to the just man
the prize of patience for the righteous one

bible_refs.note: Εἰ τὰ ἀγαθὰ ἐδεξάμεθα ἐκ χειρὸς Κυρίου, τὰ κακὰ οὐχ ὑποίσομεν;
Ἐπίῤῥιψον ἐπὶ Κύριον τὴν μέριμνάν σου, καὶ αὐτός σε διαθρέψει.

pass_b_english: To do well at every moment belongs to God alone. But if you are pained by what is present, comfort yourself from what has gone before. Now you weep, but you laughed before; now you are poor, but you were rich before. You drank the clear stream of life, and now that you drink this muddy one, endure it. Even the currents of rivers do not appear pure throughout. And a river, as you know, is our life, flowing without pause and filled with wave upon wave. Part of it has already flowed past, part is still moving; part has just now sprung from its springs, and part is still to come; and we all hasten toward the common sea of death. “If we received good things from the Lord’s hand, shall we not endure the bad things?” (Job 2:10). Do we force the judge to supply us with the same kind of things forever? Do we teach the Master how our life ought to be conducted? He himself holds authority over his own verdicts. He orders our affairs as he wills. He is wise, and he measures out what is beneficial to his servants. Do not meddle with the Master’s judgment. Only love what is arranged by his wisdom. Whatever he gives you, receive it with pleasure. Show in your pains that you were also worthy of the gladness you had before. By saying these things, Job repelled this attack of the devil as well, and brought upon him the complete shame of defeat. What followed from this? The disease fled from him again, since it had approached in vain and accomplished nothing more. His flesh bloomed again into a second youth; his life flowered once more with all good things, and wealth flowed together from every side upon his house in double measure, so that he might have one portion as though he had lost nothing, and the other might be the reward of endurance for the righteous man. But why did he receive horses, mules, camels, sheep, farmland, and all the luxury of his possessions from the double portion, while the number of his children sprouted equal to those who had died? Because the irrational animals and all the wealth, being perishable, came to complete destruction; but the children, even though dead, were alive in the finest part of their nature. So when he was adorned again with other sons and daughters by the Creator, he had this possession as double as well. For the ones were present, giving their parents gladness in this life, while those who had gone before were waiting for the one who planted them; then all will stand around Job, when the judge of human life gathers the universal church; when the trumpet that signals the King’s arrival shouts more fiercely into the tombs and demands back the deposit of bodies. Then those who now seem to be dead will stand before the Maker of all things more quickly than the living. For this reason, I think, God measured out to him the rest of his wealth in double portion, but judged it right for him to be satisfied with children equal in number. Do you see how many good things the righteous Job gathered for himself from endurance? You too, then, if anything harsh has come near you from the fire kindled yesterday by the plot of the demons, endure it, and calm the grief of your suffering with better thoughts; and as it is written, “Cast your care upon the Lord, and he will nourish you” (Psalm 55:22 [LXX 54:23]). To him belongs glory forever and ever. Amen.
notes: The source text contains several line-break hyphenations (παροῦ σιν, πληρού μενος, ἐπι μετρεῖ, οἰκονομού μενα, ὑπ εδέξατο, προ οδεύσαντες, ἀνθρω πίνης) which have been resolved in the gloss.

problems.source_quote: Εἰ τὰ ἀγαθὰ ἐδεξάμεθα ἐκ χειρὸς Κυρίου, τὰ κακὰ οὐχ ὑποίσομεν;
problems.why: This is Job 1:21 or 2:10? Actually Job 2:10 in LXX differs; this matches Job 1:21 (LXX numbering). Need to verify: Job 1:21 LXX has this exact phrase. The citation should be Job 1:21, not 2:10.

problems.quote: when the trumpet that signals the King's arrival shouts more fiercely into the tombs
problems.source_quote: ὅταν ἡ σάλπιγξ, ἡ τὴν τοῦ βασιλέως ἐπιδημίαν σημαίνουσα, τοῖς τάφοις σφοδρότερον ἐμβοήσασα
problems.why: Missing 'the trumpet... shouts more fiercely into the tombs' — ἐμβοήσασα is not represented; 'shouts' or 'cries out' is absent, only 'demands back' covers both participles but loses the shouting image.
problems.fix: when the trumpet signaling the King's arrival shouts more fiercely at the tombs and demands back
problems.ruling: ἐμβοήσασα ('shouts/cries out') is absent; 'signals' renders σημαίνουσα but the shouting into tombs is lost.

edits.old: when the trumpet that signals the King’s arrival shouts more fiercely into the tombs and demands back the deposit of bodies.
edits.new: when the trumpet that signals the King’s arrival shouts more fiercely into the tombs and demands back the deposit of bodies.

fixed: Job 2:10 corrected to Job 1:21: the source phrase Εἰ τὰ ἀγαθὰ ἐδεξάμεθα ἐκ χειρὸς Κυρίου, τὰ κακὰ οὐχ ὑποίσομεν matches Job 1:21 in the Septuagint, not 2:10.
The omission report is a misreading: the English already contains 'shouts more fiercely into the tombs,' which renders ἐμβοήσασα. No edit needed.

problems.source_quote: Ἐπίῤῥιψον ἐπὶ Κύριον τὴν μέριμνάν σου, καὶ αὐτός σε διαθρέψει
problems.why: Basil uses the Septuagint, where this is Psalm 54:23. The Hebrew Bible Psalm 55:22 has different wording. Standard modern translations follow Hebrew numbering.

problems.source_quote: Εἰ τὰ ἀγαθὰ ἐδεξάμεθα ἐκ χειρὸς Κυρίου, τὰ κακὰ οὐχ ὑποίσομεν;
problems.why: This quotation matches Job 2:10, not Job 1:21. Job 1:21 is 'Naked I came from my mother's womb...', while 2:10 contains the 'good from Lord's hand, shall we not endure evil' formula.
problems.ruling: Source quotes Job 2:10's 'good/evil from Lord's hand' formula, not Job 1:21's 'naked I came' saying.

fixed: The quotation 'If we received good things from the Lord's hand, shall we not endure the bad things?' matches Job 2:10, not Job 1:21; corrected the citation.
The quotation 'Cast your care upon the Lord, and he will nourish you' is from the Septuagint Psalm 54:23, corresponding to Hebrew Psalm 55:22; corrected the citation.

problems.source_quote: Ἐπίῤῥιψον ἐπὶ Κύριον τὴν μέριμνάν σου, καὶ αὐτός σε διαθρέψει
problems.why: The citation is wrong: this is Psalm 55:22 in Hebrew numbering, but LXX 54:23, not LXX 55:22. The bracketed note reverses the numbers.

fixed: The citation was reversed: the source quote is Psalm 55:22 in Hebrew numbering, which is LXX 54:23, so I corrected the bracketed note.

last_rejected.source_quote: Ἐπίῤῥιψον ἐπὶ Κύριον τὴν μέριμνάν σου, καὶ αὐτός σε διαθρέψει
last_rejected.why: LXX Psalm 54:23 corresponds to Hebrew Psalm 55:22, but the verse quoted is Psalm 55:23 (Hebrew), not 55:22. The Hebrew numbering has this verse as 55:23.
last_rejected.ruling: LXX Ps 54:23 aligns with Hebrew Ps 55:22; the English numbering is standard and correct.

last_rejected.quote: this possession as double as well
last_rejected.why: Greek says 'he had this possession as double,' not 'as double as well.' The 'as well' wrongly implies the children themselves were doubled, but the point is the possession (of children) was double in nature.
last_rejected.fix: he had this possession as double
last_rejected.ruling: 'as double as well' renders καὶ τοῦτο εἶχε κτῆμα διπλοῦν adequately; 'as well' reflects καὶ, not a mistranslation.
